paragraphs: Bad weather is coming back on Monday, the last day of the bank holiday weekend. Met Éireann has new yellow warnings.
There is a wind warning for 11 counties from 5pm to midnight. They are Carlow, Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Kilkenny, Mayo, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow.
There is also a rain warning for Cork and Kerry from 4pm to 10pm. Some roads may flood. The ground is already very wet after Storm Boelo.
Big waves will hit the coast. Trees may fall. Driving and cycling will be hard.
Stay away from the sea. Do not drive into flood water. Put garden chairs and other loose things inside before the evening.
Met Éireann has put new yellow weather warnings in place for Monday, just after Storm Boelo left thousands of homes without electricity over the weekend.

A wind warning is in force from 5pm until midnight on Monday for 11 counties: Carlow, Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Kilkenny, Mayo, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow. Very strong and gusty south to southwest winds are expected. A rain warning also covers Cork and Kerry from 4pm to 10pm, after heavy rain there overnight.

The ground is already full of water, so more rain could cause local flooding, especially in the south-west and west. Rivers will stay high into Tuesday. Strong winds, high tides and big waves may also bring flooding to the coast. Gale warnings are in place at sea until 2am on Tuesday.

People should expect difficult travel, fallen trees and branches, and objects blown around. Outdoor events may be cancelled; Cork County Council has already called off a Halloween event at Mallow Castle.

Drivers should slow down and leave more space. Never drive into flood water, because less than 30cm of moving water can lift a car. Keep away from the coast, and tie down garden furniture before the evening.
Met Éireann has issued fresh Status Yellow wind and rain warnings for Monday, bringing a stormy end to the bank holiday weekend after Storm Boelo cut power to tens of thousands of homes.

A wind warning covering Carlow, Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Kilkenny, Mayo, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow is valid from 5pm until midnight, with very strong and gusty south to southwesterly winds. A separate rain warning for Cork and Kerry runs from 4pm to 10pm, following a night of heavy downpours in the region.

With soils already saturated, further rain could lead to localised flooding, particularly in the southwest and west, and river levels are expected to remain high into Tuesday. Onshore winds combined with high tides and a storm surge also raise the risk of coastal flooding, while gale warnings remain in force at sea until 2am on Tuesday.
Forecasters expect difficult driving and cycling conditions, fallen trees and flying debris. Several outdoor events have been cancelled, including a family Halloween event at Mallow Castle.

Motorists are advised to slow down, double their stopping distance and never enter floodwater of unknown depth. The public is urged to avoid exposed coastal areas and to secure loose items such as garden furniture.

Met Éireann has issued a fresh round of Status Yellow wind and rain warnings for Monday, threatening to wash out the final hours of the bank holiday weekend in the wake of Storm Boelo, which knocked out power to tens of thousands of homes.

Very strong, gusty south to southwesterly winds will batter Carlow, Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Kilkenny, Mayo, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow from 5pm until midnight. Meanwhile, Cork and Kerry face a further spell of heavy rain between 4pm and 10pm, on the heels of torrential overnight downpours.

Because the ground is already waterlogged, additional rainfall could trigger localised flooding, notably in the southwest and west, where rivers are set to remain swollen into Tuesday. Onshore gales coinciding with high tides and a surge also heighten the risk of coastal overtopping, and gale warnings at sea persist until 2am on Tuesday.
Treacherous travel conditions, toppled trees and airborne debris are anticipated, and organisers have already scrapped a number of outdoor events, among them a Halloween gathering at Mallow Castle.

Motorists should reduce speed, double their stopping distance and steer clear of floodwater of unknown depth. The public is also urged to shun exposed coastlines and to tie down garden furniture and other loose objects.

Met Éireann has issued further Status Yellow wind and rain warnings for Monday, which are likely to disrupt the concluding hours of the bank holiday weekend, following Storm Boelo, which left a substantial number of homes without electricity.

A wind warning affecting Carlow, Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Kilkenny, Mayo, Waterford, Wexford and Wicklow is in effect from 5pm until midnight, with very strong and gusty south to southwesterly winds forecast. In addition, a rain warning for Cork and Kerry applies between 4pm and 10pm, subsequent to considerable overnight rainfall.

As soils are already saturated, additional precipitation could consequently result in localised flooding, particularly in the southwest and west, where river levels are projected to remain elevated into Tuesday. Furthermore, the combination of onshore winds, high tides and a storm surge substantially increases the likelihood of coastal flooding, and gale warnings remain in force at sea until 2am on Tuesday.

Motorists are advised to reduce their speed, double their stopping distance and avoid floodwater of uncertain depth. Members of the public are also urged to avoid exposed coastal areas and to secure garden furniture and other loose objects.
